items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: John Malachi on piano... And I was playing trumpet... That was that band.

ctx.x: Who was in it when you were there?

It wasn't as big a band as... That band wasn't; it was a smaller band. Paul Jones and Harry Curtis, who was playing first alto. John Malachi on piano. Tommy on drums. Benny Fonville playing bass. Chester Brown was playing guitar. Good one, too; he died. Good guitar player, man. He was way ahead of his time. Chester Brown on guitar. And Pete Jones playing trombone. Reds McCurry was playing trumpet. And I was playing trumpet and Jefferson also. We had Pete Jones on trombone. And that was it. That was that band.

items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Osie Johnson, Leonard Phillips and a fellow named Harry Curtis... we formed a band, a six-piece band. We worked at this famous club... called the Crystal Caverns.

ctx.x: really became fast friends... There was one guy, Leonard Phillips -- we called him Phil. He was a trumpet player. And he and another fellow, Otto Jones... I think Otto's from Arkansas. As a matter of fact, I think they're both from Arkansas, Phil and Otto. [BOTH ARE FROM WARREN, ARKANSAS] They were older guys, and they knew all these people. They would say, "That's Ben Webster" and "That's Chu Berry" and "That's Roy Eldridge."

There was this guitar player that worked with Booker Coleman and taught me a lot about chords; his name was Sammy Woods. Just to show you how things change, and different... Roy Eldridge used to come to Washington here. When he was in town, Sammy would have his guitar, and he'd have a string around his neck, and he would go around and see Roy. Between shows, Roy would come out with his horn and a mute. And they would walk, like... The Howard Theatre was at Wilberg(?) and T Street, which is between Sixth and…
